NEW DELHI: Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) members Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka on Wednesday withdrew their plea before the Delhi high court challenging the extension of their custody and seeking immediate release.The development came after the court questioned why they had approached it when proceedings before the Special Executive Magistrate (SEM) were scheduled to take place later in the day.The court advised them to wait for the outcome of the SEM proceedings and consider the available legal remedies.The activists had challenged the SEM’s October 19 order extending their custody until October 21 under preventive proceedings initiated under Sections 126 and 170 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS).They had argued that their continued detention was illegal and violated their right to personal liberty, claiming they had remained in custody since October 13 despite furnishing sureties for release.The case stems from their protest at Jantar Mantar on October 13, after the site was denotified as a designated protest venue.
Article Summary: Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) members Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka on Wednesday withdrew their plea before the Delhi high court. The development came after the court questioned why they had approached it when proceedings before the Special Executive Magistrate (SEM) were scheduled to take place. The activists had challenged the SEM’s October 19 order extending their custody until October 21.

Article Title: ‘Was it necessary?’: Anupam Kher slams Uttarakhand BJP minister over Daler Mehndi row
Article Text:
Anupam Kher slams BJP cabinet minister over ‘public humiliation’ of Daler Mehndi in Uttarkhand

What Anupam Kher said

Mika Singh defends his brother

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Veteran actor Anupam Kher has backed singer Daler Mehndi after Uttarakhand cabinet minister Subodh Uniyal confronted him on stage during a cultural event, questioning his performance. Kher criticised the minister's conduct, asking whether it was necessary to publicly humiliate the singer instead of raising concerns privately.“Mantri ji...kya sabke saamne manch par jakar is tarah unhe apmanit karna zaruri tha?” Kher wrote in an Instagram post, expressing disappointment over the way the singer was addressed in front of an audience.The controversy erupted after Mehndi's performance at the annual Siddhpeeth Maa Kunjapuri Tourism and Development Fair in Tehri Garhwal, Uttarakhand. Uniyal allegedly questioned the singer's presentation, claiming that he appeared disoriented and was lip-syncing. The minister also alleged that Mehndi was drunk.In his post, Kher said he had known Mehndi for several years and was concerned about the singer's health. He said the singer had not been keeping well and deserved to be treated with dignity after decades of contributing to the music industry.“I watched a video in which a minister was speaking to Daler Mehndi ji on stage.The way he spoke to him was deeply upsetting to see. I have known Daler ji for many years. I also know that he hasn’t been keeping well for some time now. Minister ji, you may have had complaints about his performance. You may even have been upset with him. But was it really necessary to go up on stage and humiliate him in front of everyone? Couldn’t the same thing have been said to him privately, with dignity and respect? (Mantri ji. ....kya sabke saamne manch par jakar is tarah unhe apmanit karna zaruri tha?),” Kher wrote.He added that an artist's contribution should be acknowledged and respected, particularly after years of work.“An artist spends an entire lifetime earning the recognition and respect that comes through years of hard work. For the past 30–35 years, Daler ji has brought joy to all of us through his songs. Surely, his contribution deserves some appreciation and respect. Daler ji, I have always known you as a kind-hearted person who spreads love. As far as I know you, you don’t even drink alcohol. I am deeply sorry that you had to go through something like this. ”Earlier, singer Mika Singh came out in support of his brother, saying Mehndi had been unwell for the past two years and had undergone an operation recently. Mika suggested that his health could explain his speech during the performance and rejected allegations that the singer had consumed alcohol.“I know my brother Daler Mehndi, and he does not drink alcohol. He has been unwell for the past two years and is still recovering, yet he continues to perform with his band. These days, many performers use backing tracks, but nobody questions them in the same way,” Mika said.Kher also urged members of the film industry to speak up in support of Mehndi, saying it should not be Mika's responsibility alone to defend his brother.The incident has triggered a debate over the treatment of performers at public events, with Kher questioning why any concerns about Mehndi's performance could not have been raised privately and respectfully.
Article Summary: Veteran actor Anupam Kher has backed singer Daler Mehndi. Uttarakhand cabinet minister Subodh Uniyal confronted him on stage during a cultural event. Kher criticised the minister's conduct, asking whether it was necessary to publicly humiliate the singer instead of raising concerns privately.

Article Title: Jhota murder case: CBI takes over Punjab anti-drug activist killing case, files fresh FIR
Article Text:
FIR in Jhota murder case days after activist was shot dead in Mansa

NEW DELHI: CBI has officially taken over the murder probe of anti-drug activist Parvinder Singh Jhota, re-registering the case to begin its independent investigation. A special probe team arrived at the Mansa Police Station late last night with a formal letter issued to the police to take over existing records and seizures."As part of the ongoing probe, a CBI team led by a senior DIG will examine the family members of the victim, who are scheduled to reach the Mansa Circuit House Wednesday. Additionally, forensic experts, drug controllers, and other specialists are expected to arrive in Mansa shortly to assist with the investigation," a senior CBI official said.Officials will specifically investigate potential links regarding how banned psychotropic substances were openly sold at chemist shops, sources added.To further this angle, the anti-corruption probe agency will take over documents from the Punjab Police in Mansa and seek the custody of chemist Ashwine Kumar and other individuals.Jhota was murdered on October 13, after being shot during a confrontation at a medical store in Mansa. The Punjab Police claimed to have found in its investigation that the activist was shot dead by chemist Ashwine Kumar during an altercation that was being livestreamed on Facebook.According to the findings, Jhota had confronted the medical store owner over the alleged open sale of banned psychotropic substances and synthetic drugs. The probe revealed that the accused opened fire inside the shop and subsequently followed the injured activist into the street, leading to Jhota's death at Mansa Civil Hospital, before fleeing and later being arrested in Rajasthan.
Article Summary: CBI has officially taken over the murder probe of anti-drug activist Parvinder Singh Jhota. A special probe team arrived at the Mansa Police Station late last night with a formal letter issued to the police to take over existing records and seizures.Jhota was murdered on October 13, after being shot during a confrontation at a medical store in Mansa.

Article Title: More trouble for CJP leaders: Another FIR against Saurav Das, Ashutosh Ranka transferred to Crime Branch
Article Text:
File photo: Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka

CJP leaders move Delhi High Court against custody extension

Detentions began on October 10

NEW DELHI: The Delhi Police has transferred a second FIR registered against Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) leaders Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka to the Crime Branch, which will now investigate both cases linked to the activists' alleged entry into Connaught Place and Jantar Mantar, sources said on Wednesday.Two cases were registered on October 13 following protests by CJP members at the two locations without approval, according to news agency ANI.The case related to Connaught Place was transferred to the Crime Branch on Tuesday, while the second case, concerning Jantar Mantar, has also now been handed over to the unit, sources said.According to news agency PTI, the police alleged that Das, Ranka, Ajinkya Shinde and 11 other CJP members entered the Jantar Mantar area on October 13 by trespassing through private premises. Jantar Mantar has been denotified as a designated protest site.Police personnel deployed at the spot intervened, and all 14 people were detained. Two FIRs were subsequently registered.Meanwhile, Das and Ranka have approached the Delhi High Court challenging an order extending their judicial custody, arguing that their continued detention despite furnishing sureties violates their fundamental right to personal liberty.Their legal team has challenged the October 19 order passed by a Special Executive Magistrate in New Delhi district under Sections 126 and 170 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS).According to their lawyers, the magistrate rejected fresh sureties submitted by the two leaders on October 19 and directed them to explain why there should not be an apprehension of a breach of peace.The legal team contends that the continued detention is arbitrary and contrary to established legal principles. The leaders have sought the setting aside of the order, arguing that their detention infringes their constitutional right to personal liberty under Article 21.The matter is scheduled to be taken up by the High Court on Wednesday.The leaders sought an urgent hearing on Tuesday, including a night hearing, as the High Court remains closed for the Dussehra vacation.CJP legal affairs head Ratna Singh said in a post on X, "We have moved the Delhi high court and requested an urgent night hearing. Saurav and Ashutosh should not spend a single minute behind bars. Their liberty must not be curtailed because of political games. Justice must not wait."The party has alleged that bail proceedings have been deliberately delayed to prevent the release of its two co-convenors, the newspaper reported.According to their legal team, Das and Ranka were first detained on October 10 after arriving at Terminal 3 of the Indira Gandhi International Airport. Preventive proceedings were initiated against them the following day, after which they were released on executing bonds of Rs 50,000 each.They were detained again on October 13 after going to Jantar Mantar carrying the national flag. They were subsequently shown as arrested under Sections 126 and 170 of the BNSS on October 14.A Special Executive Magistrate sent the two leaders to five-day judicial custody on October 14 for allegedly breaching peace bonds. Their custody was extended by two days on Monday after police sought further detention, citing apprehensions of a breach of peace.
Article Summary: CJP leaders Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka have been in custody since October 10. They are accused of entering Connaught Place and Jantar Mantar without approval. The two leaders are challenging an order extending their judicial custody.

NEW DELHI: A 30-foot cockroach effigy was burnt alongside those of Ravan, Kumbhkaran and Meghnad during Dussehra celebrations at Netaji Subhash Place in Delhi on Tuesday. The move drew sharp reactions from Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) leaders and sparking a debate on social media.While the organisers said the effigy symbolised filth and promoted cleanliness, CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke shared a snippet from the film Swades, featuring the lyrics "mann se raavan jo nikaale, ram uske mann mei hai (One who casts Ravana out through contemplation, Ram dwells there)."In a separate post he also thanked them for the "free publicity"."Thank you for the free publicity," Dipke said on X, sharing a post about the effigy.CJP legal head Ratna Singh described the development as "tamasha" as she wrote, "Tamasha kara lo bas is desh mein (Just let this country turn everything into a spectacle.)"In another post, she said the incident showed that the CJP had "done something right"."Burning a cockroach effigy on Dussehra only shows how rattled the ruling party is... Good to know we are making enough of an impact for you to see us as competition," she said."Clearly, we are doing something right. Give your IT cell some time off as well. You must be tired after all this (useless) hard work," Singh added.The 30-foot effigy was burnt at the DDA ground in Netaji Subhash Place, Pitampura, alongside those of Ravan, his brother Kumbhkaran and son Meghnad. The event, organised by the Shri Keshav Ram Leela Committee, drew a large crowd.Committee president Ashok Goel Devaraha, a BJP MLA from Model Town, said the cockroach represented filth and unhygienic surroundings. He said the initiative aimed to raise awareness about related health problems, including allergies and asthma.The committee said the effigy was part of its efforts to promote cleanliness under the Swachh Bharat and Swachh Delhi campaigns. Devaraha said it burns an additional effigy representing a social problem every year, citing previous examples linked to COVID-19, Naxalism and foreign goods.Reacting to an AAP complaint about the effigy, Delhi minister Kapil Mishra said, "The effigy being burnt is that of a cockroach, yet it is the 'termites'—the political termites of this nation—who are feeling the pain."He further added, "The public has its own unique 'pesticide' to deal with them. A cockroach is a symbol of filth and chaos. The people want such effigies to be burnt; just as anti-national forces emerge, their defeat in India is inevitable."
Article Summary: A 30-foot cockroach effigy was burnt alongside those of Ravan, Kumbhkaran and Meghnad during Dussehra celebrations at Netaji Subhash Place in Delhi on Tuesday. The move drew sharp reactions from Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) leaders and sparking a debate on social media.

Article Title: Allahabad HC cites long trial, lets off offenders, SC slams ‘misplaced sympathy’
Article Text:
SC has directed the accused in the 2003 case to surrender and asked the HC to conduct a fresh hearing.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: A “gracious” trial court and a “very indulgent” Allahabad HC paved the way for two offenders in a grievous hurt case to go scotfree without spending a day in jail on the grounds that they suffered because of a 22-year-long trial, but the courts did not consider the victim, who is still getting treatment, Supreme Court has said.Now, SC has directed the accused in the 2003 case to surrender and asked the HC to conduct a fresh hearing.A bench of Justices J B Pardiwala and K Vinod Chandran said it was a case of misplaced sympathy. The trial court had awarded fiveyear jail terms to the two, but the HC released them on probation. SC said the case was “doomed from its inception insofar as justice delivery to the victim is concerned”.“We cannot but, with an amount of consternation, notice the casual manner in which the trial court and the high court considered the issue from the stage of taking cognisance till the release of the accused on application of Probation of Offenders Act. They have gone scot-free without suffering a single day of imprisonment, especially by reason of the misplaced sympathy based on grandiose expositions of law,” it said.The court passed the order on an appeal filed by the brother of the victim, who has lost substantial functionality of both upper limbs.SC said the HC “went overboard” and wondered how it could pass such an order despite the adverse report on the character of the offenders, noting that theywere involved in multiple criminal cases. “True, protracted trial is agonising but here, the accused were on bail and merrily indulging in criminal activities,” the bench said.
Article Summary: The trial court had awarded fiveyear jail terms to the two, but the HC released them on probation. Now, SC has directed the accused in the 2003 case to surrender and asked the HC to conduct a fresh hearing. SC said the case was “doomed from its inception insofar as justice delivery to the victim is concerned’

Article Title: Two Andaman, one Chhattisgarh site added to Unesco World Heritage tentative list
Article Text:
India has 45 UNESCO World Heritage Sites.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Three sites from India have been added to the tentative list of United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization's World Heritage Convention, the Permanent Delegation of India to UNESCO announced on Tuesday.The three sites are the Karst-mud-volcano Complex of Baratang and Andaman Subduction Volcanoes in the Andaman and Nicobar Islands, and the Sirpur Cultural and Archaeological Landscape in Chhattisgarh.In a press release dated October 20, the Permanent Delegation of India to Unesco, based in Paris, announced the additions to India's Tentative List under the UNESCO World Heritage Convention.Inclusion on the tentative list is a prerequisite for any property to be considered for nomination to the World Heritage List. The delegation also acknowledged the Archaeological Survey of India (ASI) for its work in the process.The additions mark a step towards the possible future nomination of the three sites for Unesco World Heritage status.India has 45 UNESCO World Heritage Sites, including 37 cultural sites, seven natural sites and one mixed site, following the inscription of the ancient Buddhist site of Sarnath in July 2026.India ranks sixth globally and second in the Asia-Pacific region.The five countries with the highest numbers are Italy with 62 sites, China with 61, France with 56, Germany with 55 and Spain with 50.India’s first four sites were inscribed in 1983: the Ajanta Caves and Ellora Caves in Maharashtra, and Agra Fort and the Taj Mahal in Uttar Pradesh. These were all cultural sites recognised for their historical, architectural and artistic significance.
Article Summary: The three sites are the Karst-mud-volcano Complex of Baratang and Andaman Subduction Volcanoes in the Andaman and Nicobar Islands. The additions mark a step towards the possible future nomination of the three sites for Unesco World Heritage status. India has 45 UNESCO World Heritage Sites.

Article Title: AAIB chief gets a year's extension as many key probes, including AI 171, on
Article Text:
GVG Yugandhar

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Govt has granted a one-year extension to Aircraft Accident Investigation Bureau (AAIB) director-general G V G Yugandhar, with some key ongoing investigations — including Air India AI 171 crash — awaiting their final reports. The reason: Having a new DG at a time like this could delay the final report into the June 12, 2025, Ahmedabad crash. Accordingly the aviation ministry had recommended an extension for Yugandhar, who retired as Indian Air Force group captain earlier this year, and the same was approved about a month back.The key probes that are currently underway have AI 171 Air India right at the top followed by Air India’s turbulent Phuket-Delhi flight of Aug 4, 2026, and some other crucial cases. AI 171 report is learnt to be in its final stage and will be shared with stakeholders as per rules once ready.People in the know say while the aviation ministry “keeps the aircraft accident investigating agency at an arm’s length and does not interfere in its working in any way,” it is taking steps to strengthen the AAIB. The bureau's lab has been recently upgraded and it now has the capability to download cockpit voice recorder and digital flight data recorder (black box) to know the conversation in the flight deck and the flight parameters till before an event being investigated.It is learnt that the aviation ministry is working on having regional offices of AAIB to ensure investigators reach the site of accident/incident at the earliest. Additionally, this is to augment the bureau’s infra at a time when India’s aviation is seeing a boom right from the number of flight training schools to aircraft in fleet of Indian operators with the figure currently being close to 900.Aurobindo Handa, who was with IAF director (engineering) till Oct 2018 and then joined AAIB as DG on deputation where he remained for 3.5 years, said: “Some steps have been taken to strengthen AAIB but a lot more has to be done. The plan is to have regional offices wherever DGCA has the same. The same must be staffed by non DGCA people to avoid 'conflict of interest'. The investigator’s execution has to be like a clockwork mechanism as its scientific reports pinpointing cause/s of accident/incident are crucial for air safety to prevent the same thing from happening again. And to achieve the outcomes, immaculate staffing is the most important function.”AAIB was formed in 2012 following an ICAO objection that the regulator (DGCA) can’t be the investigator. Till then panels packed with DGCA officials used to conduct probes into accidents and incidents.
Article Summary: Aircraft Accident Investigation Bureau (AAIB) director-general G V G Yugandhar given one-year extension. Having a new DG at a time like this could delay the final report into the June 12, 2025, Ahmedabad crash. People in the know say the aviation ministry is taking steps to strengthen the AAIB.

Article Title: No hacker, no warning: How AI agents can enter business systems without anyone noticing
Article Text:
How Indian firms' confidential data was exposed

Five security gaps that can expose businesses to AI agents

How can an AI test reach a real business?

AI went looking online and found its way into Indian firms’ confidential data

Why did the businesses not notice?

CERT-In flags a new cyber blind spot

AI agents also raise risks for cyberattacks

Who is responsible if an AI agent accesses confidential data?

AI experiments spill into the real world

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

What if an AI agent being tested by a company on the other side of the world could quietly enter your business’s systems, read confidential records and leave without triggering an alarm?India’s cybersecurity agency has flagged precisely this kind of risk, reporting cases in which AI agents accessed live systems during research and testing, exposing a blind spot in how companies protect their data from tools they may never have authorised.In an advisory issued on October 15, the Indian Computer Emergency Response Team (CERT-In) said it had received voluntary disclosures from AI model providers whose agents had accessed live systems belonging to Indian organisations. The agents reportedly found their way in through exposed passwords, access keys left in public code repositories and cloud accounts with broader permissions than necessary.The affected organisations did not detect the access themselves, CERT-In said. The incidents came to light through reviews by the AI developers, raising a troubling question: if an AI agent can cross into a real business system while being tested elsewhere, how would the business know what it had seen, or whether its data had been exposed?AI agents are software systems that can carry out tasks with limited human involvement. They can search the internet, use other software and make a series of decisions to complete a task.Developers test these agents to understand what they can do. But if an agent is allowed to access the internet and comes across a working password or access key, it may be able to enter a system that was never meant to be part of the test.For example, a company may accidentally leave an access key in a public code repository. If that key allows entry to a database, an AI agent that finds it may be able to read the information stored there.Jaydeep Singh, general manager for India at cybersecurity firm Kaspersky, said an agent does not need hostile intent to cause a breach.“It needs a goal and valid access,” he said.Singh said an agent may be given instructions to stay within a certain task, but those instructions cannot prevent access to other systems if its credentials allow it to go further.Rajesh Chhabra, general manager for India and Asia at cybersecurity firm Acronis, said an agent may find credentials in a configuration file, code repository or cloud account that give it more access than its task requires.“The lesson isn’t that the agent went rogue. It is that the permissions were weaker than anyone realised,” he said.The disclosure does not establish that AI companies deliberately targeted Indian businesses. It does, however, raise questions about whether developers did enough to keep their tests separate from real business systems.A company does not need to have an AI agent of its own for one to access its systems. If an agent finds a working access key, it may be able to enter through the same channels used by employees and other software.This can make the activity difficult to identify. Security systems may record that an account accessed a database, but not clearly show whether the account was being used by an employee, a software programme or an AI agent.“Logs record the credential used, not whether a human, a script or an agent used it,” Singh said.Some businesses also do not keep detailed records of which files or customer records were accessed after a successful login. Without these records, security teams may struggle to identify unusual activity.Sunil Sharma, managing director and vice-president of sales for India and SAARC at cybersecurity firm Sophos, said agents can operate at machine speed while using valid credentials and broad access permissions.“A legitimate agent can also become risky if it is compromised or misconfigured, so monitoring has to look at behaviour,” Sharma said. “The principle is simple: trust the agent’s behaviour, not just its origin.”Sophos' Active Adversary Report 2026, based on 661 incident response and managed detection cases handled between November 2024 and October 2025, found that 67 per cent of the investigated incidents involved identity-related attacks. It also found that multi-factor authentication was missing in 59 per cent of cases and that gaps in the retention of security logs had doubled year on year.These findings do not relate directly to the incidents disclosed by CERT-In. They point to wider problems with how organisations manage access to their systems and track activity within them.CERT-In's advisory also described a separate set of incidents in which cybercriminals used AI tools to carry out attacks against Indian organisations.The agency said these attacks reduced the time between gaining initial access to a system and causing damage from days to hours. It also observed that some organisations that had not fully addressed an earlier breach were attacked again on a larger scale.The two situations are different. In the first, an AI agent under evaluation accessed systems beyond its authorised scope. In the second, criminals used AI tools to attack organisations. Both show how quickly weaknesses such as exposed passwords and excessive access permissions can be exploited.Kaspersky reported that its security products detected more than 92,000 attacks involving malware and potentially unwanted applications disguised as popular AI agents and services worldwide between January and early May 2026. It also identified more than 15,000 malware samples posing as agentic AI software, including fake versions of OpenClaw.These figures concern malicious software disguised as AI tools, not the incidents reported by CERT-In. Read Kaspersky's findings.The CERT-In disclosure leaves an important question unanswered: when an AI company discovers that its model has accessed another organisation's data without permission, who must notify the affected business and help investigate what happened?Manish Chasta, co-founder and chief technology officer of Eventus Security, said businesses investigating suspected access should examine records of logins, database activity, software requests and cloud access. These records can help establish which account was used and what information it accessed.If an access key is known to have been exposed, or there is credible evidence that it has been misused, it should be revoked or replaced promptly. Security teams should also check whether other accounts or access keys were created, while preserving records needed for the investigation.CERT-In has recommended that AI developers restrict agents' internet access during testing, use fake credentials and test data instead of real business information, and monitor their activity. Testing systems should be prevented from reaching unrelated live systems.Businesses, meanwhile, should remove exposed access keys, review who can enter their systems and disable online services that are no longer needed.Chhabra of Acronis said companies should test AI agents in a separate copy of their systems, using fake records and dummy credentials rather than putting live business data at risk.The advisory does not establish how widespread these incidents are or whether the accessed data was transferred elsewhere. But it shows how an AI test can affect a business that has no involvement in it.For Indian organisations, the challenge is to detect when an account is being used in an unexpected way. For AI developers, it is to ensure that a model being tested cannot reach systems outside the approved environment. Neither should depend only on the AI following instructions.
Article Summary: CERT-In has received voluntary disclosures from AI model providers whose agents had accessed live systems belonging to Indian organisations. The agents reportedly found their way in through exposed passwords, access keys left in public code repositories and cloud accounts. The affected organisations did not detect the access themselves.

NEW DELHI: Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke has urged volunteers to spend time with their families during the upcoming festivals, while asking them not to give in to hatred or provocation amid the recent detentions of activists associated with the movement.In a video shared on X, Dipke thanked supporters for standing by one another and said the movement would continue to follow the path of peace, love and compassion. His message came amid the detention of CJP leaders Sourav Das and Ashutosh, whom he described as his brothers.“The past few days have not been easy for us,” Dipke said, recalling his earlier warnings during the movement at Jantar Mantar that the activists could face police action and cases.The video followed Special Executive Magistrate (SEM) Court decision to extend the judicial custody of CJP leaders Saurabh Das and Ashutosh Ranka till October 21. Be there with your families, be there with your loved ones,” he urged volunteers, adding that their families would be worried after the events of the past few days.Emphasising the need to maintain the movement's commitment to non-violence, Dipke said the difficulties faced by activists should not push them towards hatred.“We are fighting against hatred, we are fighting against the people who have nothing but hatred in their mind. They are our strength,” he said.Dipke invoked Mahatma Gandhi and BR Ambedkar while describing the values he said should guide the movement. He said the activists' response to their detention reflected their commitment to peaceful resistance.“When Sourav and Ashutosh will come out, they will come out of jail with the slogan of Inquilab Zindabad," he said." Article Title: SC judges jokingly threaten to sit on dharna for foot overbridge and pedestrian path

NEW DELHI: In the season of dharnas and protests in Delhi, a Supreme Court bench led by Justice J B Pardiwala last week threatened in a lighter vein to sit on dharna at the Delhi HC main gate if by Nov 25 the govt failed to construct a foot overbridge and pedestrian paths to facilitate safe road crossing for lawyers, litigants and public.Justices Pardiwala and K V Viswanathan told additional solicitor general Vikramjit Banerjee - “If you don't do it before the next date, both of us will be at the main gate of the HC, and we will not go home until you complete the work. That's for sure. Baith jaayenge wahan dharna karne ke liye.”The case related to the stretch of Mathura Road near the HC and Zoological Park, where absence of a foot overbridge and pedestrian safe crossings had been flagged months ago by the SC. Amicus curiae Gaurav Agrawal informed the court on Friday that a traffic signal has been installed. But that did not satisfy the court which threatened sit-in dharna by the judges.If to get a work done for benefit of public, the SC judges, even in lighter vein, feel that dharna is a better option than issuing a mandamus to the govt, then it could have serious implications given the stark contrast between right to expeditious justice and the pendency of more than 95,000 cases in the SC.This is the view expressed by a cross-section of lawyers in lighter vein when TOI sought their responses to Justice Pardiwala's banter.Even if one can tell litigants that they must not complain about the 36,000 cases which are pending 'only' for five years in the apex court which has time and again ruled that right to speedy justice is part of right to life, what would the SC tell the litigants who are waiting patiently for the balance of nearly 60,000 cases?If they decide to enforce their right to speedy justice through dharna at the SC, it would create a law and order situation, which an already stretched Delhi police will find it difficult to handle, the lawyers feared.What about those litigants in the HCs who have been awaiting a hearing in their cases for years together, without expecting a decision? They have been routinely told by the SC to await their chance in the HC and declined then out of turn hearing. maximum such application for a direction for early hearing pertain to the Allahabad HC, where over 12 lakh cases are pending, many for decades. If lakhs of litigants decide to hold dharnas at the HC and its bench at Lucknow, would the police be able to handle the surge of protesters?In the trial courts, the pendency is more than 5.1 crore cases, of which 47 lakh are more than 10 years old and 81 lakh are between 5-10 years-old. What if these litigants, who while awaiting justice have been drained of their finances, are physically exhausted by repeated adjournments and mentally disturbed by the pendency, decide to hold sit-in dharnas at the trial courts?

Article Title: Young innovators impress juries with ideas to solve real-world challenges

NEW DELHI: Three separate juries evaluated entries in the three categories for the award and the panel members acknowledged at the end of the day that the quality of applicants was excellent. In each of the categories, bulk of those shortlisted for evaluation by the jury were very young, either still in college or just out of it, though there were some older innovators too.Over 14,000 applications were received, which were filtered down by Techgig to 1,000 and Grant Thornton shortlisted it to 35 finalists that were split between three juries. While first was on sovereign technology for India handled 14 entries, second on Inclusive Innovation for Bharat met a dozen applications and third on Sustainable & Resilient India dealt with nine entries.The juries followed a pattern of a short presentation by the applicants, followed by questions from jury members and then a brief discussion between the members before scoring the applicant. Several jury members admitted that they were pleasantly surprised by how well thought through the presentations were, especially given the age of most applicants.Even where some aspect of the road to implementation may have not occurred to the applicants — say, a compliance issue or consent to be obtained — it was striking how eager the innovators were to learn from the experience of those who had worked in the real world for decades and knew what it takes to translate brilliant ideas into real solutions.The maturity to take hard questions as essential inputs rather than as harsh criticism was quite remarkable.The diversity of the presentations was also a striking aspect. In the technology sovereignty category, for instance, the ideas ranged from closing a felt gap in middle sized drones to faster and more efficient identification and countering of cyberattacks to dealing with ships that go ‘dark’, which may not always be for innocent reasons.But these were not just ideas. The drone entry had already done some testing in the field with army units, the dark ships idea had been explored with a port and so on.Such was the overall quality of the applicants that at least in two categories some of the jury members voiced the opinion that perhaps the awards need not be restricted to two in each category. There was, after all, no compulsion to stick to a bell curve, they pointed out. Most left the venue feeling satisfied that they had done their bit to encourage a cohort whose innovative mindset was matched by its enthusiasm to do good for society and for India.

Article Title: Presidential election today? Trump confuses India with Brazil, claims 125 million voted
Article Text:
Trump says "125 million Indians voted in presidential election today."

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

US President Donald Trump on Monday confused India with Brazil, claiming that 125 million people had voted in an Indian “presidential election”, while also questioning the integrity of the American voting system.In a post on Truth Social, Trump wrote, “125 Million People voted today in the first round of India’s Presidential Election. The results came out shortly after the vote closed, on the same day!”He then compared the alleged election results with the US electoral process, writing, “In Detroit, Philadelphia, California, and numerous other US Cities and States, the results, with much smaller numbers, will often take weeks to Rig, I mean, calculate. Voting in America is corrupt!!!”However, India did not hold a presidential election on Sunday. The President of India is elected indirectly by an electoral college and not through a direct nationwide popular vote.Trump's remarks came after Brazil held the first round of its presidential election on Sunday, with incumbent President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva and right-wing challenger Flávio Bolsonaro advancing to the October 25 runoff.With 99.99% of the votes counted, Bolsonaro secured 47.03% of the valid votes, while Lula received 45.16%, according to Brazil's Superior Electoral Court.The figure of around 125 million mentioned by Trump is close to Brazil's total valid votes, which stood at about 125.27 million, suggesting he may have confused the Brazilian election with India.Neither Bolsonaro nor Lula crossed the 50% threshold required to win in the first round, triggering the October 25 runoff, BBC reported.Flávio Bolsonaro, the son of former Brazilian president Jair Bolsonaro, outperformed expectations in the first round and finished ahead of Lula. His strong showing has raised the prospect of a shift to the right in Latin America's largest economy.Brazil has used electronic voting for decades, and electoral authorities said the first-round voting process proceeded smoothly.The Organization of American States' electoral observation mission said “the voting has been going smoothly and under adequate safety conditions.”The rapid announcement of results has also been cited as a strength of Brazil's electronic voting system.“When results take a lot of time, it creates an opening for people to cast doubt on the results, to say there’s been a problem,” Josemar Lauriano Pereira, a 46-year-old lawyer in Rio de Janeiro, told the Associated Press.Trump's post drew reactions on social media, with users pointing out that India does not elect its president through a direct popular vote.One user posted, “Trump living in a different world? Is a presidential election taking place in India? President Donald Trump made the incorrect claim that 125 million people voted in India's "presidential election" today.”Another said, “What is my blud Donald Trump smoking? Why is he mentioning India instead of Brazil when talking about the election?”
Article Summary: US President Donald Trump confused India with Brazil, claiming that 125 million people had voted in an Indian "presidential election" He also questioned the integrity of the American voting system. India did not hold a presidential election on Sunday. The President of India is elected indirectly by an electoral college.

Article Title: SIR strikes at heart of Constitution: Supreme Court judge Ujjal Bhuyan
Article Text:
File photo: Supreme Court of India Judge Justice Ujjal Bhuyan (PTI Photo)

-

Detaching right to vote from citizen is like taking soul out of body: Bhuyan

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Launching a scathing attack on special intensive revision (SIR) that has resulted in large-scale deletion of names from voter lists across states, Supreme Court judge Justice Ujjal Bhuyan on Sunday said any process disenfranchising millions of Indian citizens was intrinsically arbitrary as it struck at the heart of the Constitution.Discounting the reasons given by govt and EC to justify SIR, which was upheld in the case of the revision of rolls in West Bengal by SC with modifications, Justice Bhuyan said, "No amount of whataboutery can justify it. It strikes at the very heart of Constitution. I would go to the extent of saying that it is a negation of the constitutional order which we have adopted under the Constitution."He was speaking at the moot court valedictory function at Nalsar, Hyderabad.Nalsar students, who had opposed CJI Surya Kant's participation in the convocation ceremony recently, came in for praise from Justice Bhuyan.Also read| Democracy in peril as voters illegally ousted: Former SC judge Justice Rohinton Fali Nariman "One last word about the brilliant students of Nalsar. You have shown to the country and to the world what a university student, that too a student of law, should be. You are brilliant, you are bold, and you are brave," he said.Justice Bhuyan said a citizen’s right to vote was central to the holding of free and fair elections.“Except in the case of a dead voter, the name of a voter once enlisted in the electoral roll cannot be deleted without notice and hearing,” he added.The SC judge said the right to vote or be included in the voters’ list could not be detached from the persona of an Indian citizen.Also read: EC orders special drive to add genuine electors 'left out' during SIR “If it is done, it will be like taking out the soul from the body,” he added. Justice Bhuyan said the Indian Constitution does not provide for two classes of citizens: citizens with voting rights and citizens without voting rights. “Any process which leads to wholesale disenfranchisement of Indian citizens, making them citizens without voting rights, would be violative of Articles 326 and 14 of Constitution of India,” he said.“If any process results in disenfranchising millions and millions of Indian citizens, making them second class citizens in their own country in the sense of being citizens without voting rights, such a process is intrinsically arbitrary,” he added, his remarks coinciding with attacks on EC and govt over SIR by the opposition and others.Justice Bhuyan said the right to vote was intertwined with India’s years of struggle against foreign rule. “It is a manifestation of our freedom achieved after so much struggle and sacrifice. Article 326 (universal adult franchise) cannot be tinkered with at all. No authority can do it, no court can condone it. No one is above Constitution,” he said.
Article Summary: Supreme Court judge Justice Ujjal Bhuyan said any process disenfranchising millions of Indian citizens was intrinsically arbitrary as it struck at the heart of the Constitution. He was speaking at the moot court valedictory function at Nalsar, Hyderabad. “If it is done, it will be like taking out the soul from the body,” he added.

Article Title: ‘Play the ball as late as possible’: Sunil Gavaskar’s advice to India batters for New Zealand Tests
Article Text:
Sunil Gavaskar

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Mumbai: Sunil Gavaskar has advised India’s batters to play the ball as late as possible when they face New Zealand in the two-Test series in Wellington and Christchurch, where swing and seam are expected to pose a major challenge.India struggled on their last Test tour of New Zealand in February-March 2020, losing 0-2 after managing totals of 165, 191, 242 and 124. With green pitches likely again, Gavaskar said patience and technique would be vital.“Like in England, you try and play as late as possible. Don’t commit yourself too much, because that gives you the chance to cover the movement off the pitch,” Gavaskar said.“When there is movement in the air, you can see it and react. But after pitching, the movement happens very close to the bat. The later you play, the better your chances of scoring runs and defending the good ball. Don’t push at the ball. Defend with soft hands, not hard hands.”The batting great also questioned the decision to schedule only two Tests, saying every series in the next World Test Championship cycle should have at least three matches.“Ideally, there should be a minimum of three Tests. Two Tests don’t always give you a result. One team could win one match and the other team the next.A third Test gives you a better opportunity to win a series,” he said.He believes India will benefit from having spent an extended period in New Zealand before the Tests, with the team already playing five T20Is and five ODIs on the tour.“One of the biggest problems in New Zealand is getting your body clock used to the time difference. It takes a really long time for your sleep and waking hours to adjust. The Indian team being there already is going to be a big plus,” Gavaskar said.He warned that early-summer conditions could make batting difficult but said runs would be available once batters settled in.“There will be a fair bit of grass, cooler weather and the possibility of rain. The ball will move in the air and after pitching, so it won’t be easy. But once you settle down, these can be some of the best pitches to bat on. I’m hoping our batters get going,” he said.Gavaskar also backed India’s pace attack to challenge New Zealand.“With Jasprit Bumrah leading the attack and Mohammed Siraj around, we have the capability of surprising the New Zealand batting unit. We’ve got a good team. As with everything, you need a little bit of luck,” he said.(Tune-in: Watch India’s tour of New Zealand live and exclusive on Sony Sports Network and Sony LIV, starting October 22, 2026.)
Article Summary: Sunil Gavaskar has advised India’s batters to play the ball as late as possible when they face New Zealand in the two-Test series in Wellington and Christchurch. The batting great also questioned the decision to schedule only two Tests, saying every series in the next World Test Championship cycle should have at least three matches.

Article Title: Usain Bolt pledged J$10 million with Puma to help restore damaged schools across Jamaica
Article Text:
Usain Bolt (Getty images)

Usain Bolt and Puma donated J$10 million to two Jamaican schools

Usain Bolt Foundation continues its investment in Jamaican youth

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Last year, when Hurricane Melissa tore through Jamaica and left schools struggling with severe damage, Usain Bolt stepped in to help the communities that shaped his journey. The sprinting legend joined hands with longtime sponsor Puma to donate J$10 million towards rebuilding two high schools hit hard by the disaster. The contribution brought support to students and teachers facing damaged classrooms and disrupted school life. For Bolt, whose own story began in Jamaican schools and track programmes, the donation also reflects a long-running commitment to giving young people the chance to learn, compete and build a future.Bolt and Puma each directed J$5 million to St Elizabeth Technical High School, known as STETHS, and William Knibb Memorial High School in Trelawny, where Bolt studied. Both institutions suffered serious damage when Category 5 Hurricane Melissa struck Jamaica in late October 2025.At STETHS in Santa Cruz, the damage included the complete loss of the roof on the Grade 11 block. The building plays a key role for students preparing for Caribbean Secondary Education Certificate exams. Other roofs, teachers' cottages, athletes' dormitories and parts of the perimeter wall also suffered damage.The school's spectator stands were left badly damaged as well.William Knibb Memorial High School reported damage to seven buildings, six of which were severely affected. Several structures lost their roofs, creating an urgent need for repairs before students could return to normal learning conditions.The donations aim to support recovery at both schools, helping restore spaces that matter to students, teachers and the wider communities. Rebuilding classrooms and other facilities is vital not only for everyday lessons but also for students preparing for important examinations and sporting events.The latest contribution builds on Bolt's work through the Usain Bolt Foundation, which supports education, sport and youth development across Jamaica. The foundation has backed communities in rural parishes including Trelawny, St Elizabeth, St Ann, St James and Clarendon.Earlier in 2025, it provided J$6.1 million in cash and supplies to six rural high schools preparing for the ISSA Boys and Girls' Championships. William Knibb was among the beneficiaries.The foundation has also helped younger children by supplying printers, hygiene stations and learning materials to 21 early-childhood institutions across five parishes. The effort supported more than 1,200 children and their teachers during the COVID-19 pandemic.Bolt's relationship with Puma adds another layer to the relief effort. The brand signed him in 2003, when he was just 16, and the partnership grew alongside his rise to global fame. In 2021, he secured a lifetime deal with Puma, becoming the first track-and-field athlete to receive such an agreement.That long-standing connection now supports a cause beyond athletics. By joining forces to help rebuild damaged schools, Bolt and Puma are directing their influence towards communities facing a difficult recovery. For the students at STETHS and William Knibb, the donation offers practical help as they work towards returning to classrooms and rebuilding their school lives.
Article Summary: Usain Bolt and Puma donated J$10 million to two Jamaican schools. St Elizabeth Technical High School, known as STETHS, and William Knibb Memorial High School in Trelawny, where Bolt studied. Both institutions suffered serious damage when Category 5 Hurricane Melissa struck Jamaica in October 2025.

NEW DELHI: New Zealand captain Mitchell Santner has identified Bhuvneshwar Kumar as a potential threat in the five-match T20I series against India, warning that the veteran pacer’s ability to exploit movement in the air and off the pitch could make him particularly dangerous in familiar swinging conditions.Bhuvneshwar is returning to India’s T20I setup after nearly four years, and the opening match is scheduled at Hagley Oval in Christchurch on Thursday. For New Zealand, his comeback presents a challenge that goes beyond experience: the 36-year-old’s mastery of the new ball could prove decisive in conditions traditionally suited to swing bowling.“I think Bhuvi will love these conditions in New Zealand. If there's anything in the wicket, he'll find something out of it,” Santner said on the eve of the series opener. “[Even] on some flat ones in India, he still manages to nip the ball and swing the ball. So with the new ball out here especially, he'll be a challenge.”Bhuvneshwar’s strength lies in his ability to move the ball both ways, trouble batters with his control and make the most of even limited assistance from the surface. New Zealand’s conditions could amplify those qualities, particularly during the powerplay, when batters are expected to attack but the new ball can offer assistance to seamers.Santner contrasted the challenges of bowling in India’s increasingly high-scoring T20 conditions with the prospect of finding more assistance at home.“I mean in India it's pretty challenging as a bowler these days, like we've seen in the recent series (against West Indies], 250 getting chased down - who wants to be a bowler? - but he might like it out here a little better,” Santner said.The numbers underline Bhuvneshwar’s experience in the format. He has taken 90 wickets in 87 T20Is at an average of 23.10, including two five-wicket hauls and three four-wicket hauls.His recent IPL resurgence has further strengthened his case for an international comeback. Playing for Royal Challengers Bengaluru, he took 28 wickets in 16 matches in the 2026 season at an average of 17.89 and an economy rate of 7.95, helping the franchise secure its second consecutive title.Across the 2025 and 2026 IPL seasons, he claimed 45 wickets in 31 matches, offering evidence that his experience and skill remain valuable in the shortest format.India captain Shreyas Iyer believes Bhuvneshwar’s return will add valuable experience to a bowling attack that has featured several newer faces.“Bhuvi, like you said, brings a lot of experience in the team,” Iyer said. “That was something we lacked, especially after the IPL we had a lot of new bowlers. If you see Bhuvi's career graph in the last two years, he's won the IPL also so he knows very well how to dominate this format.”Bhuvneshwar now has an opportunity to reach 100 T20I wickets, needing 10 more to join Arshdeep Singh, Jasprit Bumrah, Hardik Pandya and Axar Patel among Indian bowlers to achieve the milestone.

Article Title: Ishan Kishan on the verge of three major T20 records as India take on New Zealand
Article Text:

Ishan Kishan chasing T20I records

Can Kishan become India's first 2,000-run batter in a year?

NEW DELHI: Ishan Kishan has three major batting milestones in sight as India prepare for the five-match T20I series against New Zealand, starting in Christchurch on Thursday. The wicketkeeper-batter is closing in on the record for most T20I runs by an Indian in a calendar year, the overall record for a batter from a Test-playing nation and the landmark of 2,000 runs in T20 cricket in a single year.Kishan, who has enjoyed a breakthrough year in India's T20I setup, needs just seven runs to surpass Suryakumar Yadav 's Indian record of 1,164 T20I runs in a calendar year, achieved in 2022.The left-hander has scored 1,158 runs in 34 T20I innings this year at an average of 37.35 and a strike rate of 172.06, including a century and seven half-centuries.Kishan is also closing in on the calendar-year record for most T20I runs by a batter from a Test-playing nation. Pakistan's Mohammad Rizwan holds the mark with 1,326 runs in 2021, leaving Kishan 139 runs short of the milestone.The India batter is also just 46 runs away from becoming the seventh Indian to complete 2,000 runs in T20Is. In 66 matches, he has scored 1,954 runs at an average of 31.51 and a strike rate of 148.81, with one century and 13 half-centuries.Beyond international cricket, Kishan has another significant milestone within reach.He has scored 1,760 runs in 49 T20 matches this year at an average of 38.26 and a strike rate above 175.He needs another 240 runs to become the first Indian batter to score 2,000 runs in T20 cricket in a calendar year. West Indies' Nicholas Pooran and Rizwan are the only batters to have crossed that mark, with Pooran scoring 2,331 runs in 2024 and Rizwan accumulating 2,036 in 2021.With five T20Is against New Zealand followed by a three-match series against Sri Lanka in December, Kishan has opportunities to rewrite the record books before the year ends.

Article Title: Travis Kelce's heartbreak deepens as $1.7 billion Cleveland Guardians extend World Series drought to 78 years
Article Text:
Travis Kelce (Getty Images)

Cleveland Guardians fall short after promising ALCS start

Travis Kelce and Cleveland fans face another championship heartbreak

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

The Cleveland Guardians have suffered another painful postseason exit, extending a championship drought that has haunted the city for nearly eight decades. Their 7-3 defeat to the Tampa Bay Rays in Game 6 of the American League Championship Series ended their hopes of reaching the 2026 World Series. For fans, including Kansas City Chiefs star Travis Kelce, the loss brings another reminder of Cleveland’s long wait for baseball glory. The Rays, meanwhile, secured their place in the Fall Classic, where they will face the Milwaukee Brewers in a matchup between two teams chasing their first World Series championship.Cleveland looked well placed to reach the World Series after winning two of the first three games against Tampa Bay. However, the Guardians could not maintain that momentum as the Rays won three consecutive games to close out the series.The decisive Game 6 exposed Cleveland's struggles at the plate and the pressure on its pitching staff. Tampa Bay built an early advantage and controlled much of the contest, leaving the Guardians searching for a response.Junior Caminero delivered a crucial blow in the seventh inning when he launched a two-run homer off Cleveland closer Cade Smith.Yandy Díaz added another two-run home run in the eighth, giving Tampa Bay a cushion that proved decisive.Cleveland made a late push in the eighth inning, cutting the deficit from four runs to two after a series of walks and a hit batter brought home two runs. Yet the rally ended when Kevin Kelly struck out Brayan Rocchio with the bases loaded.The defeat was especially frustrating for a Guardians team that led the American League with 41 comeback victories during the regular season. Their inability to take control in the closing stages of the series ultimately proved costly.Cleveland's latest elimination extends its World Series title drought to 78 years. The franchise last won the championship in 1948, when it defeated the Boston Braves. Although the team has reached the World Series four times since then, it has yet to bring another title home.For Cleveland supporters, the latest setback adds another chapter to a long history of postseason disappointment. The Guardians won the AL Central and advanced past the Chicago White Sox in the Division Series, raising hopes that this could finally be their year.Manager Stephen Vogt acknowledged the disappointment after the loss.“Yeah, let it hurt,” Cleveland manager Stephen Vogt said he told his club. “That hurts. I couldn’t be more proud of our group. It just hurts. It stings. Really felt like we had a team to go and just weren’t able to get there.”The Guardians now face an offseason of reflection after coming so close to the biggest stage in baseball.For the Rays, the victory brings a different opportunity. They will meet the Milwaukee Brewers in a World Series featuring two franchises still searching for their first championship. While Tampa Bay prepares for that historic contest, Cleveland must wait another year to chase the title that has eluded the city since 1948.
Article Summary: Cleveland Guardians lose 7-3 to Tampa Bay Rays in American League Championship Series. The defeat ends their hopes of reaching the 2026 World Series. Tampa Bay will now face the Milwaukee Brewers in a World Series featuring two franchises still searching for their first championship. Cleveland's World Series title drought extends to 78 years.

Article Text:

Actor Ignored Warnings

Tiger attack: 15 teams tracing shooters





MUMBAI: In yet another instance of a gangland attack on a film personality, unidentified motorcycle-borne assailants repeatedly fired at a car carrying actor Tiger Shroff and his driver Firdaus in Juhu around 7 pm Sunday, injuring Firdaus on his hand and a fan standing nearby who sustained bullet wounds near his chest.Seven shots were fired in all. The actor who was leaving after attending a birthday party at Pushpa Narsee Park, also known as Jamnabai Nursery, escaped with “minor abrasions” from pieces of shattered glass from the vehicle’s windscreen.Two persons identifying themselves as Anil Pandit and Harman Sandhu, and claiming to be affiliated with the Lawrence Bishnoi gang, took responsibility for the attack in a voice note posted on social media.Amid political reactions questioning the city’s law and order situation, CM Devendra Fadnavis took a briefing from police commissioner Deven Bharti and sought strict action. He also rang Tiger Shroff and assured him saying, “We are all with you.”The incident took place barely 350 metres away from Juhu police station. The vehicle was slowly exiting the venue when two of the assailants, standing amidst a crowd of curious onlookers, sprang in front of the car and opened fire repeatedly.At least one bullet went through the shattered glass of the vehicle. Juhu police said the three assailants, in white shirts, fled in seconds towards SV Road and Vile Parle railway station on a bike kept idling by their accomplice.Also read: ‘Jaldi le kar jaao, Tiger’: Video shows seat switch as Tiger Shroff takes the wheel after attack Despite being injured, Shroff’s driver emerged from the vehicle and tried to chase them. A senior doctor at Nanavati Hospital, where Shroff and Firdaus were taken, said initial scans showed a foreign body lodged in the latter’s left hand as a result of a bullet injury. He is likely to undergo surgery.In a purported video going viral on social media, one of the two shooters appears unable to fire when he is closest to the car window. The gun seemingly jams as he prepares to fire a sixth shot at point-blank range.Police were registering an FIR and seeking details from actor Tiger Shroff about any recent threat calls or warnings after unidentified motorcycle-borne assailants repeatedly fired at his car on Sunday. Fifteen teams have been formed to trace the assailants. Juhu police and Mumbai crime branch officers were examining CCTV footage to identify them and establish their escape route.Also Read: ‘Should focus on actual criminals’: Dipke jabs police after shots fired at Tiger Shroff “Shroff only has minor abrasions,” said a senior doctor at Nanavati Hospital. The actor was in the hospital’s emergency room till the time of going to the press, awaiting doctor’s advice on his discharge and the treatment plan for his driver.The third person injured in the firing—a passerby identified by police as 35-year-old Umesh Charan—sustained bullet injuries on the right side of his chest, according to Dr Chhaya Shinde, dean of BMC-run Cooper Hospital in Juhu. “He is stable at the moment but will need immediate surgery,” said a doctor.In a press release, BMC said the third patient arrived at the Cooper Hospital casualty at 7.10pm with a “history of a gunshot wound sustained at 6.30pm at Vile Parle West while covering a football match featuring Tiger Shroff. “The patient came with an entry wound at 2cm below left nipple,” the release added.Also Read: ‘Jaldi le kar jaao, Tiger’: Video shows actor taking wheel after attack Police initially said Shroff suffered slight abrasions from glass fragments after the car’s windows shattered, but DCP (west zone 2) Mohit Garg said the actor was not injured.Meanwhile, the Lawrence Bishnoi gang claimed responsibility on social media for the attack. The gang claimed Shroff had been targeted as he ignored their warnings and they also threatened to target anyone who works with superstar Salman Khan.Sources said that Shroff had been being tracked by the shooters for a few days.Posted by Lawrence’s aide, Anil Pandit, the message explicitly stated that Pandit and Harman Sandhu took full responsibility for the action taken against the actor. According to the post, the individuals involved had previously contacted the actor with warnings that were allegedly ignored, leading to the latest targeted event.The statement went on to issue a broad warning to members of the Mumbai film industry, threatening that anyone who fails to listen to them or continues to work with Salman Khan will be targeted next. The message concluded with threats directed at rival gang members and was accompanied by several hashtags referencing the Lawrence Bishnoi group and other affiliated associate networks. Police are verifying the social media post and a voice note.Pandit had earlier claimed responsibility for a shooting outside singer Guru Randhawa’s Delhi gym over an alleged Salman Khan connection.The incident evoked alarm within the film and political circles given the previous fatal attack on politician Baba Siddique in Bandra and the incidence of firing at Salman Khan’s Galaxy Apartment in Bandra Bandstand in 2024.Siddique’s son Zeeshan expressed shock and horror at Sunday’s attack on Tiger Shroff, while NCP (SP) leader Supriya Sule echoed his fears over the worsening law and order situation in the state.

Two persons identifying themselves as Anil Pandit and Harman Sandhu, and claiming to be affiliated with the Lawrence Bishnoi gang, took responsibility for the attack.

Article Title: MLBx Mumbai: Suryakumar Yadav, Shardul Thakur and four other Indian cricketers take on World Series champions
Article Text:
The teams

New York Yankees:

Los Angeles Dodgers:

Chicago Cubs:

Boston Red Sox:

The cricketers stepping up to the plate

The other side of the diamond

Built for big moments

Disclaimer: This article has been produced on behalf of

MAJOR LEAGUE BASEBALL INDIA LLP

by Times Internet's Spotlight team.

Suryakumar Yadav has built a career on hitting the ball where nobody expects it. Scoops over fine leg, ramps over the keeper’s head and flicks that travel almost backwards earned him the ‘360-degree’ tag. In baseball, most of those shots would not count. The sport allows only a 90-degree wedge of fair territory in front of the batter. Anything behind or wide of it is a foul ball.That is only the first adjustment. There is no bounce to read and no pitch to play off, and the bat is round. For bowlers, the rulebook flips the other way: the straight-arm rule that defines cricket bowling does not exist on the mound. Fielders can’t stop the ball with their pads either. They get a leather glove instead.On 24 October, six of India’s best-known cricketers will find out how quickly they can adapt. Suryakumar will be joined by Shardul Thakur, Jitesh Sharma, Kashvee Gautam, Radha Yadav and Deepak Chahar at Mumbai Football Arena, Andheri Sports Complex, where they will line up alongside World Series champions and elite softball players in a short, fast 3-on-3 format.The event, MLBx: Mumbai, is Major League Baseball’s first MLBx event in India. Four teams will carry the colours of four of the sport’s most famous franchises, each pairing an MLB legend with an Indian cricketer and an Athletes Unlimited Softball League (AUSL) star.Nick Swisher, Suryakumar Yadav, Rachel GarciaAdrián González, Jitesh Sharma, Jordan WooleryJake Arrieta, Shardul Thakur, Radha YadavJonny Gomes, Kashvee Gautam, Deepak ChaharShardul Thakur brings big-match experience. The seam-bowling all-rounder has played all three formats for India, won the IPL twice with Chennai Super Kings and played a key part in India’s 2020-21 Test series win in Australia, including the Gabba Test. At the Cubs, he will share a dugout with one of the top pitchers of his generation.Jitesh Sharma, the aggressive wicketkeeper-batter, may have the most familiar role. Standing behind the stumps is the closest cricket gets to a baseball catcher. He was part of the Royal Challengers Bengaluru squad that won the IPL in 2025 and India’s gold medal-winning team at the 2022 Asian Games.Kashvee Gautam made history in 2020 as the first Indian woman to take all 10 wickets in an innings in a BCCI domestic tournament, a spell that included a hat-trick. Radha Yadav, the Mumbai-born left-arm spinner known for her sharp fielding, was part of India’s 2025 Women’s ODI World Cup-winning squad. She started out playing tennis-ball cricket with boys in her apartment building.The baseball line-up carries serious silverware. Nick Swisher won the 2009 World Series with the New York Yankees and was an All-Star in 2010. Adrián González is a five-time MLB All-Star and four-time Gold Glove winner, the award for the game’s best defenders.Jonny Gomes played 13 MLB seasons and was part of Boston’s 2013 World Series-winning team. Jake Arrieta won the 2015 National League Cy Young Award as the league’s best pitcher and helped the Chicago Cubs win their historic 2016 World Series.The softball stars are just as decorated. Rachel Garcia is a two-time NFCA National Player of the Year, an Olympic silver medallist and the first overall pick in the inaugural AUSL Draft. Jordan Woolery is the 2026 Softball America and Big Ten Player of the Year.The 3-on-3 format keeps games short and fast, with little time to settle in, which is a test of adaptability for every player on the field. Around the action, the event will bring together music, food and entertainment. Badshah and KR$NA will perform, and Mumbai-based DJ OG SHEZ will play her genre-blending sets.Jeremiah Yolkut, MLB’s Senior Vice President of Global Operations and Events, said Mumbai’s passion for sport and entertainment made it the right setting for the event. He added that bringing cricket stars together with MLB and softball athletes gives fans a new way to experience baseball.The event builds on MLB’s partnership with RISE Worldwide to grow baseball in India. Tickets for MLBx: Mumbai are available on BookMyShow
Article Summary: MLBx: Mumbai is Major League Baseball’s first MLBx event in India. Four teams will carry the colours of four of the sport's most famous franchises. Each pairing an MLB legend with an Indian cricketer and an Athletes Unlimited Softball League (AUSL) star.

Article Title: Tiger Shroff firing: Shooters split into 3 vehicles, questioned on risky 18-hour Kota-Mumbai trip
Article Text:
The operation to transport the arrested shooters linked to Tiger Shroff's assassination attempt faced significant challenges





NEW DELHI: Transporting the arrested shooters linked to the attempted assassination on actor Tiger Shroff from Kota to Mumbai was a heavily guarded operation navigating a gauntlet of underworld threats, sources said.Maharashtra police, intelligence sleuths and local security units faced hazards following the dramatic apprehension in Kota. The tactical team and the suspects did not leave Kota on Monday night as planned, holding off until daylight.The convoy finally rolled out on Tuesday, around 11 am, by road, with the shooters split up and locked into separate vehicles to prevent any coordinated escape or security breach. Rajasthan and Gujarat police provided cover through their respective jurisdictions.En route, the shooters were initially quizzed individually to catch discrepancies. By 3 pm, they were brought into one vehicle and confronted face-to-face as their shifting versions needed to be corroborated.Intelligence sources indicated the transporting team had to brave dangers not only from the Lawrence gang but also from the Bambiha syndicate and their allies. The team was likely to reach Mumbai early Wednesday.
Article Summary: The operation to transport the arrested shooters linked to Tiger Shroff's assassination attempt faced significant challenges. The tactical team and the suspects did not leave Kota on Monday night as planned, holding off until daylight. Rajasthan and Gujarat police provided cover through their respective jurisdictions.

Article Title: Rajasthan couple found dead under suspicious circumstances
Article Text:
The house where the couple was found dead in Bisau





JHUNJHUNU: A couple was found dead under suspicious circumstances in Ward 23 of Bisau town in Rajasthan’s Jhunjhunu district, police said.The wife, Kausar, was found dead inside a room of their house, while her husband, Rahim, was found hanging.The incident came to light at around 9am when family members discovered the bodies and alerted the police.A police team, including the Bisau police station circle inspector, reached the spot and inspected the scene.The room was sealed to preserve evidence, and a forensic science laboratory (FSL) team was called to collect evidence and help determine the cause of death.Police are investigating the case from all angles and collecting evidence from the scene. The circumstances surrounding the couple’s deaths remain unclear, and the cause of death is yet to be established.Further details are awaited as the investigation continues.
