Article Title: 'I try to emulate his technique': Temba Bavuma reveals Sachin Tendulkar influence after career-best 179
Article Text:
Sachin Tendulkar and Temba Bavuma (Agency Image)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

South Africa captain Temba Bavuma has revealed how batting great Sachin Tendulkar has influenced his technique, explaining how he has tried to adapt the Indian legend's approach to suit his own game.Bavuma made the admission after scoring a career-best 179 against Australia in the second Test at St George's Park, helping South Africa recover from 110/6 to post 425/9 declared.Asked about the similarities between his technique and that of Tendulkar, one of his heroes, Bavuma said he had consciously tried to incorporate aspects of the former India batter's approach, particularly his movement and ability to play the ball close to his body."Yeah, I mean, I try to emulate my technique to his. I mean, I'm obviously not a big guy. I'm not really going to get any big strides in. I try to be efficient in terms of my movement. Sometimes it gets me into trouble. But I think for me, that's generally what works. I try to play the ball as close to my body as possible," Bavuma said.The South African skipper's 179, which came off 334 balls, was his highest Test score, surpassing his previous best of 172 against the West Indies in 2023. He admitted that the innings was particularly satisfying given his recent struggles to find rhythm."Yeah, definitely one of my better ones. I think looking at the situation of the game, and I think personally as well, I found myself a lot in those type of situations, coming in early, trying to manage myself to kind of scramble through to a 50 or 60, but I think what was nice and the ability just to take it even further and make it count," he said.Bavuma also spoke about the challenge of facing Australia's formidable bowling attack, which includes several highly ranked Test bowlers. Having failed to make a significant contribution in the first Test, he was keen to make amends."So, I mean, we got a taste of it in the first Test, and we kind of knew what was up for us. So I think for me, obviously not being able to contribute from the first Test and then coming in here in the second Test, I think that was a big thing on my mind. But yeah, I was glad I was able to put in a good contribution for the team," he said.The 36-year-old credited his work in the nets for helping him rediscover his touch after a difficult run through the ODI series and the first Test."I think I just haven't had any rhythm, to be honest with you. I kind of struggled with rhythm through the ODI series, even coming up to the first Test. So I think it was just a case of just trying to find a feeling.It can be a bit tricky when you haven't played for months. Yeah, I was just trying to go into the nets and just trying to find the feeling that I kind of had last year," Bavuma said.Bavuma's innings was supported by Marco Jansen 's 85 and Simon Harmer 's 82, with the latter adding 183 runs with the captain. Praising their contributions, Bavuma said both batters played important roles in turning the innings around."Very brave innings from him," Bavuma said of Jansen, while he praised Harmer for showing "a lot of application" and felt the all-rounder was unlucky to miss out on a century.With South Africa having fought back into the contest, Bavuma said the batting unit had done its part and the responsibility now rested with the bowlers.
Article Summary: South Africa captain Temba Bavuma reveals how Sachin Tendulkar influenced his technique. Bavuma made a career-best 179 against Australia in the second Test at St George's Park. The 36-year-old helped South Africa recover from 110/6 to post 425/9 declared.

Article Title: Dabba calls, ‘Dunkey’ route and a US dream: Inside the Randeep Malik, Anil Pandit network behind Tiger Shroff firing
Article Text:
Actor Tiger Shroff was shot at in Mumbai, causing investigators to probe connections to Lawrence Bishnoi's gang





MUMBAI: The firing at actor Tiger Shroff in Mumbai may have exposed a wider network allegedly linking Lawrence Bishnoi gang’s US-based operative Randeep Malik to gangster Anil Pandit, who has claimed responsibility for the attack.Investigators are probing Malik’s role in the conspiracy, with sources indicating that Pandit and alleged shooter Rehan Ansari had reported to him until a few months ago.Malik, considered close to Lawrence Bishnoi and his brother Anmol, is believed to operate at a senior level within the network, handling planning and target selection, according to sources. Pandit, who allegedly worked under Malik, was recently given an independent role and linked to the faction groomed by Anmol Bishnoi, sources said.The investigation has also brought into focus the gang’s alleged use of concealed communication systems, international escape routes and promises of a life abroad to recruit young men for criminal assignments.According to investigators, Pandit had allegedly planned the attack for around two-and-a-half months, recruited three men and transferred Rs 37,000 to Ansari to execute the assignment. Communication allegedly took place through voice-over-internet-protocol (VoIP) calls.In underworld parlance, “dabba calls” refer to VoIP-based communication routed through multiple connected phones and speakers at different locations to conceal the caller’s identity and physical location. Sources said Pandit had previously managed such communication arrangements for Malik and was trained by him to handle the network’s covert operations.Pandit’s alleged rise within the syndicate was also linked to the promise of an overseas future. Sources said he was sent to California through the “Dunkey” route, an illegal migration method, months after the murder of Punjabi singer Sidhu Moose Wala. His journey was subsequently held out as a success story to younger recruits, including Ansari, sources alleged.Investigators suspect the promise of money, overseas travel and a better life was used to draw vulnerable youths into the gang’s operations. Ansari, 18, had reportedly studied until Class 9 before dropping out because of financial difficulties. He was learning welding in Gurugram before allegedly joining the network. He had also been named in FIRs linked to motorcycle theft and an Arms Act case in Sonipat, and had spent time in jail, where he allegedly came into contact with hardened criminals.Ansari’s mother, Shamshida, told the media that her son should be punished if found guilty, but those who allegedly lured him into crime should also be held accountable. She said he had left home around 20 days before the firing after a man promised him Rs 2 lakh and a job.The three alleged shooters — Ansari, Phool Singh, 18, and Hrithik Roshan, 22 — were arrested aboard the Pune-Jaipur Express in Kota on Monday. They were brought to Mumbai on Wednesday and taken to the Anti-Extortion Cell after a medical examination for interrogation. A court granted police 48-hour transit remand.The firing took place around 7pm on Sunday, October 18, in Juhu, when Shroff was leaving a football club. He escaped unhurt, while his driver sustained injuries. Investigators said the shooters had monitored the actor’s movements through social media posts, videos and reels shared by him and his fans. They allegedly surveyed the playground for around 10 days and had planned an attempt on October 11, but Shroff did not turn up.The Mumbai Crime Branch has said Shroff was not the shooters’ original target. According to the agency, they initially intended to target Salman Khan but shifted their focus to Shroff, whom they believed would be easier to reach because of comparatively lower security.The probe is also examining whether the attack was part of a wider attempt to spread fear in the film industry. The Crime Branch has been asked to review the security of potential targets and prepare a list of Bollywood personalities who may face threats. Salman Khan, Ranveer Singh, Rohit Shetty, Aamir Khan and Ayush Sharma are among those who have previously received threats.Separately, Delhi Police’s Special Cell arrested four more people — Kunal, 21, Sumit, 19, Radha, 23, and Babita, 23 — in an alleged weapon-supply and logistics module linked to the attack. The court granted Mumbai Police three days’ transit remand for the four.Investigators allege that Kunal collected a pistol and 20 rounds of ammunition from Amritsar on Pandit’s instructions and persuaded Radha to carry the weapon to Mumbai. Radha and Babita travelled from Delhi on October 15 and reached Dadar on October 17. A minor boy allegedly collected the bag containing the weapon near their hotel. Police are investigating the alleged roles of the accused and their links to the shooters.The forensic team has recovered seven bullet casings or projectiles reported to have been fired, which have been sent for ballistic examination. The two firearms allegedly used in the attack are yet to be recovered.
Article Summary: Lawrence Bishnoi gang's US-based operative Randeep Malik linked to gangster Anil Pandit, who has claimed responsibility for the attack. Investigators are probing Malik’s role in the conspiracy, with sources indicating that Pandit and alleged shooter Rehan Ansari had reported to him.

Article Title: ​​Sambhajinagar set to celebrate Dasara today
Article Text:
Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar

:





As Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar was in full festive mode on the eve of the Dasara festival on Monday, markets in Gulmandi, Shahgunj, Aurangpura and Cidco bustled with shoppers buying new clothes and booking vehicles among other activities. Electronics stores also reported bookings for delivery, as the day is considered auspicious for new beginnings.Flower vendors reported heavy demand for marigold garlands even though the flowers fetched a low price of around Rs40 per kg for sellers.The festival of Dasara, which marks the victory of good over evil and concludes the Navaratra festival, will be celebrated with Shastra Puja during Vijay Muhurat in the afternoon and Ravana dahan after sunset. Many families will perform Seemollanghan and exchange “apta” leaves as gold during the evening.“Dasara festival is a time to seek blessings of Goddess Durga and family elders and relatives. The festive occasion facilitates brief reunion of friends and relatives, which is an added joy,” Shubhada Kulkarni, an entrepreneur, said.The burning of the effigy of demon king Ravana has been scheduled at Ram Lila ground, CIDCO N-7 and HUDCO N-11 and Waluj among other areas of Sambhajinagar on Tuesday evening.At N-11 HUDCO, the highlight will be the tableaux of Lord Ram, Sita, Lakshman and an 11-foot Hanuman, accompanied by a 100-member ‘Vanar Sena’ of children and volunteers, according to organisers.

Article Title: Mumbai-bound traffic hit after hatchback catches fire on Vashi Creek bridge
Article Text:
The driver immediately pulled the car over to the roadside after noticing smoke emanating from the engine.





NAVI MUMBAI: Vehicular traffic from Navi Mumbai towards Mumbai was disrupted for around 30 minutes after a hatchback caught fire while crossing the Vashi Creek Bridge on Friday at around 7.30pm.The driver escaped unhurt. He immediately pulled the car over to the roadside after noticing smoke emanating from the engine. However, the fire soon engulfed the entire vehicle, leaving it completely charred.Vashi traffic police alerted the Vashi fire brigade, which reached the spot within 15 minutes. The charred vehicle was later towed away by a crane, following which traffic movement returned to normal.Sunil Kadam, senior inspector of the Vashi traffic unit, said the driver was identified as Sumit Bhikaji Kadam.“At around 7.45pm, we received a call from one Rahul, whose full name is not known, informing us that a car had caught fire on the Mumbai-bound lane of the Vashi Creek Bridge,” said AV Sisode, the on-duty fireman at Vashi fire station.“In the meantime, we also received a call from the Vashi traffic police and immediately rushed to the spot with a fire tender. The Mumbai fire brigade team had also reached the spot as there was some confusion over the jurisdiction,” Sisode said.The fire was subsequently extinguished, and the Vashi fire brigade team returned to the station at around 8.30pm.
Article Summary: The driver immediately pulled the car over to the roadside after noticing smoke emanating from the engine. The fire soon engulfed the entire vehicle, leaving it completely charred. The charred vehicle was later towed away by a crane, following which traffic movement returned to normal.
